judged_text: The new dedicated add_members endpoint still skips usernames that do not resolve to a user and then returns success_json, so a request where every username is mistyped reports success while adding zero members. An admin typing 'bob, fred ' or misspelled names into the new Add-members input sees a success result and a refreshed list without the intended users, with no feedback about which usernames were dropped; for a PR whose stated purpose is 'proper handling of group memberships' this silent-drop behavior is under-scoped.

An admin typing 'bob, fred ' or misspelled names into the new Add-members input sees a success result and a refreshed list without the intended users, with no feedback about which usernames were dropped; for a PR whose stated purpose is 'proper handling of group memberships' this silent-drop behavior is under-scoped.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code iterates `usernames.split(",")` and only calls `group.add(user)` when `User.find_by_username(username)` succeeds; unresolved (and untrimmed, e.g. `' fred '`) usernames are silently skipped. It then returns `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds (which it typically will even if no users were added), so a request where all usernames are invalid/whitespace will report success with zero membership changes and no feedback about dropped entries. This is a real, diff-grounded UX/edge-case gap rather than a verifiable runtime failure.
